name: Sena
notes: Sena (Chisena/Cisena, Nuclear Sena, Guthrie N.44), Bantu language spoken along the lower Zambezi valley in Mozambique (Sofala/Zambezia provinces) and adjoining Malawi. Five vowel qualities a/e/i/o/u. Rich affricate and aspirate inventory: plain vs aspirated stops (p/ph, t/th, k/kh) and a series of affricates (bv, ps, pf, dz, ts, tsh, ch). The voiced bilabial and dental stops are implosive [ɓ, ɗ] by default; plain plosive [b, d] occurs only in a handful of words (Guérois 2024). Labialized sibilants sw/zw (/sʷ, zʷ/) may surface as retroflex [ʂ, ʐ] for some speakers. ⟨ng'⟩ marks the bare velar nasal /ŋ/. Prenasalized consonants occur after homorganic nasal noun-class prefixes but are not written as fixed digraphs the way Nguni/Nyanja mb/nd are, since the nasal is a separate morpheme. Unlike most Bantu languages, Sena has no phonemic tone; it instead has a predictable stress/accent system on the penultimate syllable of the phrasal domain (Guérois 2024), which is not marked in the standard orthography.

sources.author: Guérois, Rozenn

ancestors.notes: Sena branch of Bantu (Guthrie N.40), within Atlantic-Congo.

location.notes: Approximate centre of the lower Zambezi valley Sena-speaking area, Mozambique.
